cur:objects-freising-hodegetria-ivory.summary: The Virgin is shown in half-length holding the Christ Child on her left arm and pointing to him with her right hand, while two small busts of angels or saints appear in the upper corners. The Child, robed like an adult, sits upright and blesses. This is the Hodegetria ('She who shows the way'), in which Mary directs the viewer to her Son as the way to salvation.
facts: The Hodegetria type was named after a famous icon kept in the Hodegon monastery in Constantinople (tradition).
The Freising museum label describes the plaque as Byzantine, around 1000.

cur:objects-bm-baptism-of-christ-ivory.summary: John the Baptist, bearded and wearing a rough garment, lays his hand on the head of the young, naked Christ, who stands in the waters of the Jordan; the dove of the Holy Spirit descends from above, and angels attend with cloths. A small reclining figure at the bottom represents the river Jordan itself, a survival of classical personification. The panel shows the moment when Christ was revealed as the beloved Son.
facts: Early Christian images of the Baptism often show Christ as a small, youthful, naked figure and include a personification of the river Jordan, as here (type).
